correctness.rationale: For fixed r≥1 and independent uniform binary length-n strings with d_n a_nr→lambda, greedy matching makes a single fixed r-pattern absence probability a_nr=2^-n sum_{j=0}^{r-1} binom(n,j). For distinct patterns u,v, the joint greedy automaton has at most r-1 loop-capable states on live paths (otherwise they agree at every coordinate), hence O_r(n^(r-2)) jointly avoiding binary words and pair absence o(a_nr), including r=1 exactly zero. Single-row probability generating functions have rare-event expansion 1+a_nr sum_u(t_u-1)+o(a_nr); raising to d_n yields 2^r independent Poisson(lambda) coordinate misses. Coordinate zeros give Binomial(2^r,e^-lambda) common r-patterns; a_(r-1)/a_r→0 and a_(r+1)/a_r→∞ sandwich maximum LCS into {r-1,r} (empty subsequence for r=1). Independent exact enumeration and greedy DP checked one-pattern and paired-avoidance cases r≤4. Finite checks are not the asymptotic proof.

evidence: Published one-word universality-index law gives marginal distribution of all-short-pattern coverage of one word; other LCS works give estimates for fixed-number many-string constants.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A single-word universality-index distribution is not the joint per-pattern missed-event asymptotic for exponentially many independent input strings; marginal universality alone cannot establish asymptotic Poisson coordinate independence.
